source.title: Disentangling Latent Shifts of In-Context Learning with Weak Supervision

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether adapter fine-tuning on ICL-generated pseudo-labels lets a student outperform its ICL teacher, but uses the same underlying model as teacher and student rather than a separate weaker supervisor and stronger student. It does not compute PGR.
record.gate_note: The paper reports task scores for WILDA students and standard ICL teachers, including in-domain and cross-dataset evaluations. These results bear on whether the student beats the teacher. The paper does not report PGR or a strong model trained on true labels. Table 2 reports variability rather than the student-versus-teacher performance outcome and is not included. The WILDA variants are not naive fine-tuning comparisons of the auxiliary-loss, ensemble, or loss-variant methods in V2.
record.test_reason: The study trains a LoRA student on an ICL teacher's pseudo-labels and compares it with that teacher across three models and many tasks. This bears on V1's core result that a student trained on a weaker supervisor's labels beats the supervisor. It is a new setting: the teacher is the same model with 16 labeled demonstrations in context, not a separate smaller model. No strong-on-true-labels ceiling or PGR is reported, so it is not T1. It is not T4, because student-versus-teacher performance is a central reported result (Sections 3.2 and 4).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that the WILDA student consistently outperforms its ICL teacher, which they call weak-to-strong generalization. They attribute it to pseudo-label correction and coverage expansion, based on the Figure 2 analysis on Llama 3 and aggregated GLUE. They also report better stability, near-OOD transfer and efficiency than standard ICL, PBFT, ICV and Batch-ICL.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ICL predictions from the same model instance as pseudo-labels and trains a LoRA adapter on unlabeled queries; the student and teacher have the same underlying model, and no true-label strong-model ceiling or PGR is measured.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported task scores vary by task and model; the paper also reports that WILDA-S is generally more stable than WILDA-F and WILDA-R, but those stability comparisons are not student-versus-teacher performance rows here.

fits_no_version.finding: Student correction rate falls with distance to the nearest correctly pseudo-labeled training neighbour (point-biserial −0.968 ID, −0.916 OOD). Pseudo-label correction rises over training epochs, and WILDA has a lower approximated Lipschitz constant than ICL or PBFT (Figure 2a–d, Llama 3, aggregated GLUE).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In self-distillation from an ICL teacher, per-example student-over-teacher gains are predicted by representation-space proximity to correctly pseudo-labeled points (coverage expansion / pseudo-label correction).

record.problems: The teacher and student are the same model instance with the adapter toggled, so the study does not test a distinct weaker supervisor against a stronger pretrained student. It reports task scores rather than PGR and does not include a strong model trained on true labels to establish the ceiling. The experiments use three model families and selected benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Table 2 reports standard deviations for ordering stability rather than the student-versus-teacher performance measure; other comparisons of WILDA variants and baselines were not extracted as separate rows.

untested.parts: No distinct weaker supervisor or larger student; the teacher is the same model with demonstrations in context. No strong-model-on-true-labels ceiling, so PGR cannot be computed.
No auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensemble or loss variant is compared with naive fine-tuning. WILDA-F/S/R differ in demonstration handling.
Supervisor and student size are not varied independently. No PGR across tasks or sizes is reported.
No tests of exploiting uncheckable errors or of correlated errors. Near-OOD transfer reports raw scores, not PGR change.
No new theory; existing theory (Wei et al., Lang et al.) is only cited.

missing.what: WILDA-S vs standard ICL teacher at n = 4, 8 and 32 demonstrations on all GLUE and MMLU tasks. The student exceeds the teacher in every cell.
WILDA-S 0/32 and 0/16 vs 32-shot ICL teacher; the student exceeds the teacher on all nine tasks.
WILDA-S with |Dunlab| = 200 and 500 (Llama 3). Scores rise slightly over |Dunlab| = 100 but no teacher comparison row is given in this table.

record.verdict_notes: The 'weak' supervisor here is the same LLM with demonstrations in context, and the student is that LLM plus a LoRA adapter without demonstrations. This is closer to context distillation or self-training than to the original small-to-large setup. The supports label should be read as student-beats-teacher in that setting only. No row bears on V2–V6.

versions.untested_parts: The student and teacher share the same base-model architecture and model instance; the paper does not test a distinct strong pretrained student fine-tuned on labels from a distinct weaker model, and does not report PGR or a strong-on-true-labels ceiling.
No auxiliary confidence loss, ensemble of weak supervisors, or loss-variant comparison against naive fine-tuning is reported.
The study varies base model and task and reports task scores, but does not report PGR or test what predicts PGR, including representations.
Cross-dataset generalization is evaluated, but the paper does not report PGR changes under distribution shift or test weak-model-uncheckable exploits or correlated-error effects.
No new theoretical result establishes conditions under which a student must beat its supervisor.
No vision or other non-language modality is tested.

relationships.condition: Same-model ICL teacher (16-shot) vs WILDA-S LoRA student; Llama 3 8B, Phi 3 mini, Llama 2 7B; GLUE, MMLU MATH/MISC and ARC-Challenge in-domain, plus near-OOD GLUE pairs.
relationships.reason: The student beats its ICL teacher in every comparison: ID gaps of +2.5 to +12.7 points (r01–r28) and near-OOD gaps of +1.7 to +5.0 (r29–r40). There is no true-label ceiling or distinct weak model.
relationships.display_finding: Students exceeded their in-context teachers by 2.5–12.7 points in distribution and 1.7–5.0 points under nearby distribution shifts.

source_check.reason: WILDA-S exceeds its ICL teacher throughout the named comparisons. The label holds, but its reason should give ID gains of +2.3 to +12.7 points, including r20; near-OOD gains are +1.7 to +5.0.

labels.condition: Same-model ICL teacher (16-shot) vs WILDA-S LoRA student; Llama 3 8B, Phi 3 mini, Llama 2 7B; GLUE, MMLU MATH/MISC and ARC-Challenge in-domain, plus near-OOD GLUE pairs.
labels.reason: WILDA-S exceeds its ICL teacher throughout the named comparisons. The label holds, but its reason should give ID gains of +2.3 to +12.7 points, including r20; near-OOD gains are +1.7 to +5.0.

relation.reason: Directly compares the student trained on teacher outputs with that teacher on held-out ID and near-OOD tasks.

tranche.reason: Tests student-over-supervisor gains in a new setting: the same base model acts as an ICL teacher and a query-only LoRA student.

source_check.notes: This is same-model self-distillation; no distinct stronger pretrained student or true-label ceiling is evaluated, so PGR is not established. The explicit ID significance claim covers Llama 3 and Phi 3, not Llama 2.

statements.correction: In-domain gains across Tables 1, 6 and 7: +2.3 to +12.7 score points. Minimum: Llama 2 SST, 89.8 → 92.1 (Table 6, r20). Maximum: Llama 2 RTE, 69.2 → 81.9 (Table 6, r19). Near-OOD gains across Tables 3 and 10: +1.7 to +5.0 points.
statements.problem: The in-domain lower bound excludes Llama 2 SST, whose gain is +2.3 points. The near-OOD range is correct.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: WILDA-S versus standard 16-shot ICL on the reported ID tasks and ARC-Challenge, and cross-dataset evaluations
reader_labels.reason: WILDA-S scores exceed the standard ICL teacher in each listed comparison (r01–r40). This supports the student-beats-teacher effect in the tested same-model teacher/student setup; the study does not establish positive PGR against a true-label ceiling.
